modules.title: Capstone: Production SQL
modules.goal: Ship a complete, safe and observable SQL feature from schema to runbook.

topics.title: Requirements
topics.simple: Feature ko measurable requirements me todo.
topics.pro: A production SQL feature starts with the questions, freshness, volume, access and recovery requirements.

example.sql: -- requirement: monthly enrollment count, refreshed hourly, read-only dashboard

topics.title: Schema Design
topics.simple: Schema requirements ko tables aur keys me badle.
topics.pro: The schema reflects entities, relationships, constraints and the expected query grain.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE enrollments (student_id BIGINT REFERENCES students(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, course_id INTEGER REFERENCES courses(id), enrolled_on DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE, PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_id));

topics.title: Index Plan
topics.simple: Indexes real queries se justify karo.
topics.pro: An index plan lists the top queries, their predicates and the smallest indexes that support them.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_course_date ON enrollments (course_id, enrolled_on);

topics.title: Query Design
topics.simple: Query ko grain, filters aur joins ke saath likho.
topics.pro: A production query states its grain, filters early, joins on indexed keys and avoids unnecessary columns.

example.sql: SELECT course_id, COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) AS students FROM enrollments WHERE enrolled_on >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days' GROUP BY course_id;

topics.title: Transactions
topics.simple: Multi-step writes ko atomic banao.
topics.pro: A production write uses a transaction, validates the affected count and commits only after verification.

topics.title: Security
topics.simple: Feature ko least privilege aur RLS ke saath ship karo.
topics.pro: Production access uses a dedicated role, minimal grants and row-level policies for tenant or user data.

example.sql: GRANT SELECT ON enrollment_report TO reporting_role;

topics.title: Migrations
topics.simple: Schema change ko expand-contract se deploy karo.
topics.pro: A production migration is versioned, tested, lock-aware and reversible or forward-fixable.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contact_email TEXT;

topics.title: Monitoring
topics.simple: Errors, latency aur lag monitor karo.
topics.pro: Monitoring covers query latency, error rates, replication lag, lock waits and disk growth.

example.sql: SELECT query, mean_exec_time FROM pg_stat_statements ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC LIMIT 10;

topics.title: Performance
topics.simple: Plan aur measurement se optimize karo.
topics.pro: Performance work starts from a baseline plan, changes one thing and verifies the new runtime.

example.sql: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM enrollments WHERE course_id = 10;

topics.title: Testing
topics.simple: Unit, integration aur data tests likho.
topics.pro: Tests cover query results, constraint behavior, permissions and migration paths against realistic data.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments WHERE course_id = 10;

topics.title: Documentation
topics.simple: Schema, queries aur runbooks document karo.
topics.pro: Documentation explains the grain, owners, refresh cadence, access rules and recovery steps.

example.sql: -- enrollment_report: one row per course, refreshed hourly

topics.title: Incident Response
topics.simple: Failure par detect, contain, recover, learn.
topics.pro: An incident runbook detects the issue, contains impact, restores service and records a blameless follow-up.

example.sql: SELECT pid, state, wait_event FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle';

topics.title: Capacity Planning
topics.simple: Growth ko measure karke plan karo.
topics.pro: Capacity planning tracks table and index growth, connection counts and IOPS against expected growth.

example.sql: SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('enrollments'));

topics.title: Data Retention
topics.simple: Old data ko policy ke saath archive karo.
topics.pro: Retention detaches or deletes old partitions and archives them according to legal and product requirements.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE events DETACH PARTITION events_2024;

topics.title: Access Review
topics.simple: Privileges ko regularly review karo.
topics.pro: An access review removes stale roles, excessive grants and unused credentials.

example.sql: SELECT rolname, rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles;

topics.title: Backup and Restore
topics.simple: Feature ke data ke liye restore test karo.
topics.pro: A production feature confirms its data is covered by backups and restores within the recovery targets.

example.sql: pg_restore -d brocode_test brocode.dump

topics.title: Release Checklist
topics.simple: Schema, code, tests, monitoring aur rollback ready karo.
topics.pro: The release checklist verifies migrations, compatibility, permissions, observability and rollback before deploy.

example.sql: -- release: migration, code, smoke test, monitor

topics.title: Post-Launch Review
topics.simple: Launch ke baad metrics aur incidents review karo.
topics.pro: A post-launch review compares actual latency, errors and data quality with the plan and records follow-ups.

example.sql: SELECT query, calls, mean_exec_time FROM pg_stat_statements ORDER BY calls DESC LIMIT 10;

topics.title: Production Anti-Patterns
topics.simple: SELECT *, missing WHERE aur long transactions avoid karo.
topics.pro: Common production anti-patterns are unbounded queries, missing predicates, long transactions, over-indexing and untested migrations.

example.sql: SELECT id, name FROM students WHERE id = $1;

topics.title: Capstone Delivery
topics.simple: End-to-end feature ko production standard par ship karo.
topics.pro: The capstone combines schema, indexes, queries, transactions, security, migrations, monitoring, tests and a runbook.

example.sql: SELECT c.title, COUNT(DISTINCT e.student_id) AS students FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.title ORDER BY students DESC;

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Requirements in a production query.
interview.answer: A production SQL feature starts with the questions, freshness, volume, access and recovery requirements. Key rules: Define the questions. State freshness. Estimate volume. Name the users.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Schema Design in a production query.
interview.answer: The schema reflects entities, relationships, constraints and the expected query grain. Key rules: Model entities. Add keys. Add constraints. Index relationships.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Index Plan in a production query.
interview.answer: An index plan lists the top queries, their predicates and the smallest indexes that support them. Key rules: List top queries. Match predicates. Measure usage.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Query Design in a production query.
interview.answer: A production query states its grain, filters early, joins on indexed keys and avoids unnecessary columns. Key rules: State grain. Filter early. Join on keys. Select only needed columns.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Transactions in a production query.
interview.answer: A production write uses a transaction, validates the affected count and commits only after verification. Key rules: Begin. Modify. Verify. Commit or roll back.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Security in a production query.
interview.answer: Production access uses a dedicated role, minimal grants and row-level policies for tenant or user data. Key rules: Dedicated role. Minimal grants. RLS where needed.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Migrations in a production query.
interview.answer: A production migration is versioned, tested, lock-aware and reversible or forward-fixable. Key rules: Version it. Test it. Set lock_timeout. Plan rollback.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Monitoring in a production query.
interview.answer: Monitoring covers query latency, error rates, replication lag, lock waits and disk growth. Key rules: Track latency. Track errors. Alert on lag.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Performance in a production query.
interview.answer: Performance work starts from a baseline plan, changes one thing and verifies the new runtime. Key rules: Baseline. Read plan. Change one thing. Measure.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Testing in a production query.
interview.answer: Tests cover query results, constraint behavior, permissions and migration paths against realistic data. Key rules: Test results. Test constraints. Test permissions. Test migrations.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Documentation in a production query.
interview.answer: Documentation explains the grain, owners, refresh cadence, access rules and recovery steps. Key rules: Document grain. Document owners. Document runbooks.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Incident Response in a production query.
interview.answer: An incident runbook detects the issue, contains impact, restores service and records a blameless follow-up. Key rules: Detect. Contain. Recover. Review.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Capacity Planning in a production query.
interview.answer: Capacity planning tracks table and index growth, connection counts and IOPS against expected growth. Key rules: Track growth. Forecast. Test at volume.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Data Retention in a production query.
interview.answer: Retention detaches or deletes old partitions and archives them according to legal and product requirements. Key rules: Define retention. Archive. Verify deletion.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Access Review in a production query.
interview.answer: An access review removes stale roles, excessive grants and unused credentials. Key rules: List roles. Review grants. Remove stale access.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Backup and Restore in a production query.
interview.answer: A production feature confirms its data is covered by backups and restores within the recovery targets. Key rules: Confirm coverage. Test restore. Measure RTO.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Release Checklist in a production query.
interview.answer: The release checklist verifies migrations, compatibility, permissions, observability and rollback before deploy. Key rules: Migration ready. Tests pass. Monitoring ready. Rollback ready.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Post-Launch Review in a production query.
interview.answer: A post-launch review compares actual latency, errors and data quality with the plan and records follow-ups. Key rules: Compare metrics. Review incidents. Record follow-ups.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Production Anti-Patterns in a production query.
interview.answer: Common production anti-patterns are unbounded queries, missing predicates, long transactions, over-indexing and untested migrations. Key rules: Bound queries. Use predicates. Keep transactions short. Test changes.

interview.q: Module 36 · Explain Capstone Delivery in a production query.
interview.answer: The capstone combines schema, indexes, queries, transactions, security, migrations, monitoring, tests and a runbook. Key rules: Design. Build. Test. Secure. Monitor. Document.

debug.title: Unbounded query
debug.fix: SELECT student_id, course_id FROM enrollments WHERE enrolled_on >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days';
debug.error: The query scans and returns everything

debug.title: Missing WHERE
debug.fix: UPDATE students SET marks = 0 WHERE id = 1;

debug.title: Long transaction
debug.fix: Keep the transaction open only around the database work.
debug.error: Locks and snapshots are held during the wait

debug.title: Over-indexed table
debug.broken: Create an index for every column.
debug.fix: Keep only indexes justified by real queries and verify usage.
debug.error: Writes slow down and storage grows

debug.title: Unsafe migration
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN email TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT md5(random()::text);
debug.fix: Add nullable, backfill, then set NOT NULL.
debug.error: The table can rewrite under a long lock

debug.title: No permissions test
debug.broken: GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_user;
debug.fix: Grant only the needed tables and verify with the application role.
debug.error: The app can read and write everything

debug.title: No monitoring
debug.broken: Deploy and wait for a user report.
debug.fix: Add latency, error and lag alerts before launch.

debug.title: Unrestored backup
debug.fix: Restore it into a test database and verify row counts.

debug.title: Wrong grain report
debug.broken: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students JOIN enrollments ON enrollments.student_id = students.id;
debug.fix: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT students.id) FROM students JOIN enrollments ON enrollments.student_id = students.id;
debug.error: Students with multiple enrollments count multiple times

debug.title: No rollback plan
debug.broken: Deploy the migration with no reverse path.
debug.fix: Write and test a rollback or forward-fix before deploying.
debug.error: A failed release has no recovery step
